buyerStory.heading: The Buyer’s Story
buyerStory.quote: We were renting for 5 years, paying ₹20,000/month. Buying was a big step, but our EMI is now ₹22,500— and every payment builds equity. Plus, it’s our home! We have the freedom to renovate and make it truly ours. The sense of stability and belonging is unmatched. It’s an investment in our future, and we couldn’t be happier with our decision.

renterStory.heading: The Renter’s Story

contents.cardAltName: indian couple sitting on the park bench

renterStory.quote: I travel a lot for work, so renting made sense. No maintenance costs, and I can move anywhere anytime. Renting gives me freedom! Plus, I don't have to worry about property taxes or home repairs. It's convenient and fits my lifestyle perfectly.

costs.heading: What About Costs? Breaking Down the Numbers
costs.listTopPara: Wondering what costs are involved? Let’s simplify them:

list.heading: Renting Costs
list.desc:
• Monthly Rent : Depends on location, property size, and amenities—calculate based on your budget.
  • Security Deposit : Typically 1-3 months' rent, varying by landlord and city.

list.heading: Buying Costs
list.desc:
• Down Payment : 10-20% of the property value
  • Registration and Stamp Duty : Varies by state
  • Maintenance : Annual upkeep and repairs

costs.listSecPara: 💡Pro Tip : Buying has higher upfront costs, but over time, it can save you money and build wealth.

prosCons.heading:
Pros & Cons:
Renting vs Buying
prosCons.secPara:
🏠 Renting

✅ Pros:

  • Flexibility to move anytime.
  • Lower upfront costs.
  • No responsibility for repairs.

❌ Cons:

  • No equity built—money spent doesn’t come back.
  • Rent can increase every year.

🏡 Buying

✅ Pros:

  • You own your home no landlord hassles.
  • Equity growth and investment potential.
  • Freedom to renovate or customize.

❌ Cons:

  • High upfront costs (down payment, taxes).
  • Less flexibility—harder to move quickly.
